en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammapaccanīya (2), Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (2) 8.2.
Sahetukaduka (The Pair on Being With Cause)
Dependent on a state that is not accompanied by a root, a state that is not accompanied by a root arises by way of the root condition:
dependent on delusion accompanied by doubt or accompanied by restlessness, mind-produced matter [arises]; dependent on one great primary element, three [great primary elements arise].
The great elements …pe… dependent on two great elements, two great elements [arise];

dependent on the great elements, mind-originated matter, kamma-born matter, and derived matter [arise]. Dependent on a state that is not associated with a root, a state not associated with a root arises by way of root condition:
dependent on delusion accompanied by doubt or accompanied by restlessness, the associated aggregates [arise].
At the moment of rebirth-linking, conditioned by the [heart-]base, there arise the root-cause-accompanied aggregates.
Conditioned by a state that is not accompanied by root-causes, there arise states that are both not accompanied by root-causes and not without root-causes, by way of the root-cause condition.
Conditioned by a state that is not without root-causes, there arises a state that is not without root-causes, by way of the root-cause condition … three.
Dependent on a state that is neither with root-cause nor without root-cause, a state that is without root-cause arises by way of the root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither with root-cause nor without root-cause, a state that is without root-cause arises by way of the root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither with root-cause nor without root-cause, states that are both with root-cause and without root-cause arise.
By way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
Nine in the case of root, six in the case of object, five in the case of predominance …pe… nine in the case of non-disappearance.
(The section on co-nascence …pe… and the section on association should also be expanded in this same manner, just like the section on dependence.)
Root-object condition: A state that is not accompanied by a root (nasahetuka) is a condition, by way of root-condition (hetupaccaya), for a state that is not accompanied by a root.

A state that is not accompanied by a root is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is without root (naahetuka). A state that is not accompanied by a root is [a condition] for a state that is not accompanied by a root and...
And a non-root-cause phenomenon is a condition for a non-root-cause phenomenon by way of root-condition.
A non-root-cause phenomenon is a condition for a non-root-cause phenomenon by way of root-condition … three [ways].
A non-root-accompanied phenomenon is a condition for a non-root-accompanied phenomenon by way of object-condition. (Abbreviated.)

Under the condition of root (hetu), there are six; under the condition of object (ārammaṇa), nine; under the condition of predominance (adhipati), four; under the condition of proximity (anantara), nine ...

[and so on] ... under the condition of conascence (sahajāta), nine; under the condition of mutuality (aññamañña), six; under the conditions of support (nissaya) and decisive support (upanissaya), nine; under the conditions of prenascence (purejāta) and postnascence (pacchājāta), three;

under the condition of repetition (āsevana), nine; under the condition of kamma ... [and so on] ... under the condition of jhāna, four; under the condition of path (magga), three; under the condition of association (sampayutta), six; under the condition of dissociation (vippayutta), five ... [and so on] ... under the condition of non-disappearance (avigata), nine.
(As in the section on questions in the *Kusalattika*, so it should be expanded in detail.)
